children: German American Bancorp’s third-quarter earnings rose year over year as net interest income grew on improved margins, driven by lower funding costs and higher average earning assets. Wealth management fees and deposit service charges also increased, while the prior-year quarter included a gain on debt extinguishment.
² Reported as “NET INCOME”. ³ Reported as “Diluted Earnings per Share”.
: Tax-equivalent margin rose to 4.42% from 4.06%, supported by lower deposit costs and improved yields on earning assets.
: Fees increased 17%, reflecting higher assets under management and continued strong new business results.
: Loans grew $114.0M from year-end 2025, led by commercial real estate and home equity growth.
: Nonperforming assets fell to $24.0M from $29.5M at year-end 2025, partly following resolution of an acquired commercial loan without loss.
